review: The hymn is addressed to the bride of Christ (Rev 19:7–8, 21:2), so כַּלָּה is used throughout though the Arabic only says عَرُوس ('bride') once.
3:1–3:2 כִּי־כָלָה הַלַּיְלָה / וְהַשַּׁחַר קָרוֹב — Romans 13:12 (הַלַּיְלָה כָּלָה וְהַיּוֹם קָרֵב); the Arabic تَنَاهَى اللَّيْلُ is that verse, and Hebrew keeps the psalm-like brevity.
4:2 לֹא יוּכַל לְהִתְמַהְמֵהַּ — 'He cannot delay' (the Arabic لَا يَحْتَمِلُ التَّأْخِير); Hebrew uses the reflexive of מהמה, the verb of Gen 19:16 for lingering.
6:4 וְהַמַּכְאוֹבִים וְהַצָּרָה — 'and the pains and the straits'; the Arabic الضَّنْك is 'tightness/distress', and צָרָה is the biblical noun for it.
7:3–7:4 הִנֵּה לָךְ הָאָדוֹן וְהַ / כֹּל — the Arabic splits وَهَا الْـ / ـكُلُّ across the line break with a hyphen; Hebrew does the same with the definite article, because the print does.
